newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Spot prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Spot prices steady to lower.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mostly steady to lower on Monday but dealers in several locations noted a slight improvement in nearby demand.

"I have sold a few spot loads and there were some quick orders coming in," a Missouri broker said. "It has been a pleasant Monday, better than what most Mondays (usually) are." But he was uncertain if that indicated improved spot demand. "Maybe it is an aberration," he said.
One Texas dealer also said he sold some spot feed and North Texas spot millfeed was traded at $113 a ton.

But in Minnesota, spot interest in millfeeds was waning. People want corn prices to fall further and competing products, like corn gluten and sunflower meal, were available, thus pressuring millfeeds, a Minneapolis dealer said.
Corn and soybean harvesting in parts of the Midwest seemed again to be the focus. Once harvesting gets completed, he said, he expects demand to increase.
In the Carolinas, where spot prices fell $4.00 to offer at $107 a ton, activity was very quiet, a dealer said.
Northeastern mills continued to run shorter times over the weekend but spot prices remained unchanged to bid at $98 a ton and offer at $100.00 a ton, a Buffalo broker said.
